name: bounce2d
description: Landing on things and being thrown back: a Bouncer that falls onto a Bouncy surface from above leaves it with an upward speed, as a jumper does on platforms, springs and trampolines. Surfaces are one-way (the Bouncer passes through them going up and from the side) and can be single-use, break instead of bouncing, or be destroyed by the landing (a monster stomped on). A surface that breaks never costs the bounce: a Bouncer that crosses a brittle surface and a solid one in the same tick breaks the first and bounces on the second. The y axis points down, as on screen.

components.name: Bouncer
components.description: The entity lands on Bouncy surfaces. It needs a Position, a Velocity and a Collider (its box is what lands). The tick it lands, its bottom edge is compared with where it was one tick before, so a fast fall cannot go through a thin surface. bounces counts the bounces so far. fall_x and fall_y are the direction it falls in (0, 1: down, as on screen where y grows downwards; 0, -1: up; 1, 0: right; -1, 0: left): the axis with the bigger number is the one that counts, and surfaces are landed on from the side the Bouncer comes from. A game whose gravity points left gives its Bouncers fall_x -1 and fall_y 0.

components.name: Bouncy
components.description: A surface that throws a landing Bouncer back (against its fall) at strength units per second (a Collider gives its size; only the edge the Bouncer comes from counts: the top edge for a Bouncer that falls down). A Bouncer that falls onto it lands; one that moves away through it, or that passes beside it, does not. vanish removes the surface after one bounce. breaks makes it give way instead of throwing the Bouncer back: the Bouncer keeps falling, and the surface stops being Bouncy and drops at fall_speed (in the direction the Bouncer falls). A monster that dies when jumped on is a vanishing surface.

systems.name: bounce
systems.description: For every falling Bouncer, finds the highest Bouncy surface whose top edge its bottom edge crossed this tick, with the two overlapping sideways, and applies the landing: the Bouncer's Velocity points against its fall and it is put on the surface, unless the surface breaks. Runs after the movement and before collision2d.detect, so a monster that is jumped on is gone before anything counts what touches the player.
